samples.evidence: The live collaborative reader in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:460 now calls `normalizeRowHeight(Number(v))`, but nothing asserts it. Grepping packages/frontend for `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT|normalizeRowHeight` returns only the source file; packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts (a running vitest suite that already builds tables via `createTableBlock`) has no rowHeights poison case, and the same gap already exists for `normalizeListLevel` at line 506. samples.summary: Two of the four pagination "poison" values pass with or without the fix
samples.evidence: In the loop `for (const poison of [Infinity, 1e9, NaN, -1e9])`, only `Infinity` and `1e9` can fail pre-fix. The pre-fix code in table-layout.ts was `if (userHeight !== undefined && userHeight > rowHeights[r])`; `NaN > x` and `-1e9 > x` are both false, so those two iterations assert nothing about the new normalization — they hold identically on the unpatched code. Coverage is still real via the other two values.

samples.summary: `computeTableLayout` test asserts only finiteness, not the clamp value
samples.evidence: 'computeTableLayout lays a poisoned height out at finite geometry' feeds `[Infinity]` and asserts only `Number.isFinite(layout.rowHeights[0])`. A large-but-finite height (e.g. 1e9 — the OOM case the doc comment cites) would satisfy this assertion unchanged; no assertion here pins `layout.rowHeights[0] <= MAX_ROW_HEIGHT`. The 1e9 case is only covered indirectly via the pagination page-count bound.

samples.summary: The Infinity pagination case regresses as a hang/OOM rather than a clean failure
samples.evidence: `paginateWith(Infinity)` is described as 'would loop forever' pre-fix; the test declares no explicit vitest timeout, so a regression manifests as the worker spinning (and allocating a page per iteration) until the default timeout or an OOM that can take the whole file's other tests with it. A bounded guard (e.g. an explicit short `timeout` option) would make the failure diagnosable.
